The retained primary database is 314478592 bytes. context_revisions and session_events account for 89.5555 percent of allocated table/index bytes.

All 1251 contexts are distinct exact histories. Their bodies are also embedded byte-for-byte in 1251 context.revision.recorded events, copying 124729863 logical UTF-8 bytes. Legitimate history and duplicate physical representation coexist.

Positive baseline-to-crash RSS/heap and descriptor deltas mix warmup, history, collection and active crash handles. Repeated decreases and missing GC/retaining-path/CPU evidence prevent a leak or causal slowdown conclusion.

measurementSemantics.snapshotOrder: persistent-native.ts248: memoryUsage first; ps descendant census; lsof numeric FD count; SQLite file size and read-only table counts; recursive artifact content hashing. ElapsedMs was evaluated before this synchronous sample function. The fields are sequential observations, not one atomic instant.
measurementSemantics.memory: process.memoryUsage of the calling PID only. rss is process resident memory; heapUsed is V8 heap usage at that instant, including reachable values and allocations not yet collected. heapTotal is V8 heap capacity rather than retained application objects. external and arrayBuffers are separately reported counters; ArrayBuffer accounting overlaps external, so do not sum them as independent memory.
measurementSemantics.gc: runtime.gcExposed=false records absence of exposed global gc; it does not disable automatic V8 garbage collection. No GC event, full-GC boundary, heap-space generation, retained object graph or allocation rate was recorded.
measurementSemantics.fd: macOS lsof -nP -p PID -Ff counts only numeric f descriptors. It does not include every lsof mapping row. lsof/execFileSync uses measurement pipes while inspecting the worker; no file identities or descriptor categories are retained, so role or leak attribution from counts is unavailable.
measurementSemantics.process: ps recursively derives descendants and excludes the direct ps child used for observation. It is a snapshot, not a continuous subprocess census or system-wide absence proof.
measurementSemantics.cpu: No cpuUsage, resourceUsage, eventLoopUtilization, CPU profile or event-loop-delay samples exist in the report/helper. CPU utilization, CPU seconds and GC CPU fractions cannot be derived from paced elapsed time.
measurementSemantics.observerEffect: ps/lsof are synchronous; artifactMeasure reads and hashes every current artifact file; table counts and phase digest checks visit native history. Their wall-time cost and temporary allocations are not measured separately and may influence later memory samples.
measurementSemantics.workerGrowth: persistent.ts520-543 filters samples by the actual child PID and computes first baseline to last crash-ready differences. It excludes the separate recovery host. Physical SQLite delta sums primary+WAL+SHM+effects and is not the final primary-file delta.
measurementSemantics.passingMeaning: Passed verifies stated bounded workload and fault/recovery/no-replay assertions, source stability and physical cleanup. It is not a memory leak test or absolute performance guarantee; nativeCleanupConfirmed remains false and evidence is retained.

gracefulReopen.qualification: Logical Engine close/reopen shares PID, V8 heap and provider fixture. It does not reset process memory. The after sample also includes explicitly resumed queued input, one additional Run and observer call; full digest/open work occurs between samples. This is not a pure close-only retention experiment.

loadCompleteToCrashReady.qualification: Preparing the intentionally running crash command changes handles, descendants and allocations. FD35 is this phase; attributing all baseline-to-crash +7 to leaked handles is unsupported.

recoveryHostClose.qualification: A distinct PID with no matching pre-work baseline; keep separate from worker growth. Close plus retained database digest/checks changes allocations. RSS rises despite heapUsed declining slightly, illustrating that these counters do not measure the same thing.

interpretation: Reported RSS+42,811,392 bytes (40.83MiB) and heapUsed+47,231,464 bytes (45.04MiB) are baseline-to-crash-ready endpoint deltas on worker50294. Warmup, committed history, collection phase and active crash resources are mixed; no live-old-heap or leak-rate conclusion follows.

Observed worker RSS minimum83.73MiB occurs late and maximum173.44MiB occurs early. Timed RSS decreases repeatedly within both Engine instances; its descriptive OLS slope is negative in each interval even though baseline-to-crash RSS delta is positive. Neither direction can be extrapolated.

Timed heapUsed decreases31 times in Engine1 and22 times in Engine2, with adjacent sampled drops about24.92 and26.51MiB. This sawtooth-like allocated-heap sequence is consistent with transient allocation and collection, but no recorded GC event identifies each drop. Sample minima are not post-GC retained heap.

Engine1 five-minute heap minima rise across early windows while Engine2 minima fall after reopen and then vary. Therefore one monotonic lifetime retained-heap slope is not established. heapTotal settles around100MiB after warmup; that is observed capacity in this run, not a future bound.

Timed FD ranges29–31 in Engine1 and30–32 in Engine2. Baseline28, mandatory-settled29, after-reopen30 and crash-ready35 show role/phase-sensitive counts. Descriptor identities and repeated close-to-quiescent comparisons are absent; no descriptor leak attribution is defensible.

Session native history intentionally grows to797 Runs,2445 messages,1596 inputs and21746 events at crash-ready. Committed database history is not automatically all retained in JS heap: the store is SQLite-backed and context histories have finite budgets. Which objects survive or which history work allocates heavily requires GC/dominator and CPU/allocation profiles.

First-to-last timed observed cycle advancement drops from approximately18.37/min in Engine1 to8.00/min in Engine2. This is a work-progress observation on a paced, synchronously sampled workload, not CPU utilization, service latency, maximum throughput or proof that history alone caused slowdown.

Final worker exit, command PID/group absence and ownedLiveSurvivors[] are reported, and the recovery host observes0 live descendants. That supports this fixture physical cleanup scope; it does not settle unknown native command outcomes or authorize replay.
